reconcile.note: Gill treats 'twice' as a possible manuscript variant, then argues that even if genuine, all four evangelists mean the same decisive second crowing.

discrepancy.note: Strauss notes Mark alone doubles the crowing, splitting it around the first and third denials rather than a single decisive crow.

quotes.text: In Mark, it crows after the first denial ( v. 68 ), and then a second time after the third; in the other Evangelists only once, after the last act of denial.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), on Matthew 26:34 and Mark 14:30.

sides.snippet: before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.
sides.verseText: Jesus said to him, \"Most assuredly I tell you that tonight, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.\"

sides.snippet: before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.
sides.verseText: Jesus said to him, \"Most assuredly I tell you, that you today, even this night, before the rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.\"
